title: Check yourself: generic enums and their replacements

questions.stem: A monitoring library on Java 21 wants each metric to say what it measures, so a developer writes `enum Metric<V> { LATENCY, ERRORS }` and plans `Metric<Duration>` and `Metric<Long>` constants next. What does javac 21 do with this declaration?

options.text: It accepts it, since a release before 21 added type parameters to enums, and each constant is then raw
options.says: javac 21 rejects it with 'enums cannot be generic'; no release added type parameters to enums

options.text: It accepts it, since the type parameter is erased at compile time, and each constant becomes a Metric<Object>
options.says: erasure is not the obstacle: the enum declaration has no place for a type parameter, and javac refuses it

options.text: It rejects it, since the enum grammar has no place for a type parameter, and no release has added one
options.says: javac reports 'enums cannot be generic'; JEP 301 proposed generic enums and was withdrawn

options.text: It rejects it, since erasure would leave the constants without types, and only a class can keep them
options.says: erasure is not the obstacle: a generic class can hold static final constants with different type arguments

origin.section: An Enum Can't Declare a Type Parameter; JEP 301 Proposed It and Was Withdrawn

questions.stem: `final class Metric<V>` declares, in this order, `public static final Metric<Long> LATENCY = new Metric<>("latency");`, one more constant of the same shape, and `private static final Map<String, Metric<?>> BY_NAME = new HashMap<>();`. Its private constructor runs `BY_NAME.put(name, this)`. What happens the first time code reads `Metric.LATENCY`?

options.text: The class fails to compile, since a constructor can't use a static field declared after it
options.says: the class still compiles; the failure comes when it is initialized

options.text: The class fails to initialize, since the constants are created before BY_NAME is assigned
options.says: the constants' initializers run first, while BY_NAME is still null; the NullPointerException surfaces as ExceptionInInitializerError

options.text: The read succeeds with BY_NAME empty, since BY_NAME is assigned after the constants are created
options.says: the constructors run while BY_NAME is still null, so put throws before any map exists

options.text: The read succeeds with BY_NAME full, since BY_NAME is assigned before the constants are created
options.says: the constants' initializers run first, while BY_NAME is still null

origin.section: The Registry Is Yours, and So Is Its Order

questions.stem:
A sealed `Event

` permits the records `Login`, `Logout` and `Purchase`. `audit(Event e)` is a switch expression with one case per record plus `default -> "unknown"`. A teammate adds `record Refund() implements Event` to the permits, and everything is compiled together. What happens when `audit` gets a Refund?

options.text: It returns "unknown", since the catch-all branch matches it, and javac accepts the switch as it is
options.says: with a default branch the switch is already exhaustive, so adding a record changes nothing at compile time

options.text: It returns "unknown", since the catch-all branch matches it, and javac warns that Refund has no case
options.says: the default branch turns the coverage check off without a warning; Refund silently gets what the default says

options.text: It throws MatchException, since no case names Refund, and javac accepts the switch as it is
options.says: the default branch matches the Refund, so nothing is thrown

options.text: It throws MatchException, since no case names Refund, and javac warns that Refund has no case
options.says: javac gives no warning, and the default branch matches the Refund, so nothing is thrown

origin.section: A Sealed Interface of Records Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases

questions.stem: A sealed `Field<T>` permits `record Age() implements Field<Integer>` and `record Email() implements Field<String>`. A form helper reads `static <T> T blank(Field<T> f) { return switch (f) { case Age a -> 0; case Email e -> ""; }; }`. What does javac 21 do with `blank`?

options.text: It compiles, since inside each case the compiler treats T as that record's type argument
options.says: javac does not narrow T inside a case: each branch fails with '... cannot be converted to T'

options.text: It compiles, since covering every permitted record makes each branch's value acceptable
options.says: the coverage check only decides exhaustiveness; each branch's value must still be a T

options.text: It rejects the branch values, since inside each case the compiler still treats T as unknown
options.says: javac does not narrow T inside a case: both branches fail with 'cannot be converted to T'; typed behaviour belongs in a method each record implements

options.text: It rejects the switch, since covering a generic sealed interface requires a default branch
options.says: the coverage check passes; the errors are about the branch values, not about exhaustiveness

origin.section: A Sealed Interface of Records Brings Back an Exhaustive switch, but Not Typed Cases
